This is a copyable workshop prompt adapted from the named use case.
Read the goal, trigger, action, check, saved state, repetition rule, and stops in the prompt.
The percentages, time limits, and number of attempts are workshop choices, not measured results.
Goal mode continues work toward a condition. A scheduled loop starts another pass later.
Prompt limits are instructions. Use runner or platform controls for enforced time and spending ceilings.
For the scheduled example, keep the session open and confirm that the recurring task was cancelled after the third pass.
For the alert example, the alert supplies evidence; an engineer submits the goal. Automatic event delivery needs a CI integration or channel.
Do not present a slash command as a production event listener.
The complete prompt is included below.

/goal Make the full test suite at least 20% faster.
Trigger: start when I submit this goal.
Record the median of 3 full runs on the same runner.
Profile the slowest work. Change one shared cause.
Rerun the same suite 3 times after each change.
Keep changes only when tests pass and timing improves.
Preserve every test, assertion, fixture, and coverage target.
Save timings, the diff, and the next idea in loop-state.md.
Repeat until the 20% improvement is verified.
Stop after 3 changes or 25 minutes, or if blocked.
Leave a local diff for review. Do not merge or deploy.
